newsitem.title: INDIA: India cotton prices rise on export quota prospects.
newsitem.headline: India cotton prices rise on export quota prospects.

text.p: Indian cotton prices on Monday rose on expectations that the government will allow more cotton exports, dealers said.
Limited arrivals and fresh mill buying lifted prices.
In spot deals Bengal-deshi rose by 10 rupees to 900/950 rupees per maund (37.32 kg) while Punjab saw-ginned moved up by 40/50 rupees to 1,550/1,680 rupees per maund.
Gujarat Kalyan (medium-staple) lifted by 400/500 rupees to 12,700/12,900 rupees per candy (355.56 kg).
"New crop arrivals in the western and northern parts of India also remained lower today on account of unseasonal rain and cloudy weather," one broker said.
Sentiments at the close remained firm amid limited supplies while traders complained of a shortage of good quality cotton.
